html:
The Awajún, also called Aguaruna, are an Amazonian people of northern Peru, living along the upper Marañón River and its tributaries the Cenepa, Nieva and Santiago. They are one of the largest Indigenous peoples of the Peruvian Amazon.

They speak a Chicham (Jivaroan) language, close to those of the Shuar, Wampis and Achuar. Like them, they kept their independence against the Inca Empire and then the Spanish, whose towns in the region in the 1500s did not last. They lived in scattered households, growing manioc and hunting in the forest. In 2009 Awajún and Wampis protesters blocking a road near Bagua clashed with police over laws opening the Amazon to oil and logging. More than thirty people died, and the laws were repealed.
